source_document.body:
UPS is hiring 100,000 seasonal workers across hundreds of U.S. locations for the 2026 holiday shipping season . The company also announced changes to package security , tracking and pickup ahead of the rush.
What’s Related
Temporary employees will help sort, move and deliver packages. UPS said many applicants can receive a job offer in less than seven minutes, and some seasonal positions can lead to permanent jobs.
For shippers , the holiday preparations include a new Protected Delivery service that requires recipients to give drivers a PIN before receiving eligible packages. UPS also expects to deliver more than 4 billion packages equipped with radio frequency identification, or RFID , technology by the end of 2026.
The company is adding or updating automated facilities in Denver, St. Paul, Syracuse, and Portland. According to UPS’s announcement, the changes will help it maintain delivery performance during the year's busiest shipping period.

Hiring for the holidays
UPS’s hiring website says seasonal jobs typically run from October through December and have a set end date. Positions can be part-time or full-time, and some shifts start early in the morning or at midnight.
The jobs cover several parts of the delivery process. Warehouse workers sort and move packages, while driver helpers ride with delivery drivers and help deliver packages to customers without driving the truck.
Seasonal support drivers make deliveries using their own vehicles. UPS’s description says those workers receive mileage reimbursement, with a phone stipend available in some locations.
More advanced package tracking
RFID uses radio signals to identify tagged packages as they move through UPS facilities and vehicles. The company says the technology gives customers more precise tracking information.
In its April rollout announcement, UPS said it installed RFID sensing equipment in all of its U.S. package delivery vehicles and delivery facilities. At that time, the company also said packages shipped through more than 5,500 UPS Store locations carried the technology, including customer returns.
Kurt Goodwin, customer experience executive at electronics retailer Crutchfield, said the tracking helps reduce questions from customers. “For Crutchfield, that means fewer customer concerns, fewer tracking-related contacts, and greater confidence during the busiest shipping period of the year.”
A PIN before handoff
Protected Delivery adds a verification step at the doorstep: The recipient must provide a secure PIN before the driver releases the package. UPS describes the service as an option for eligible shipments, including high-value purchases and sensitive deliveries.
UPS is also adding pickup scheduling features and status alerts. Its holiday shipping options include returns through Happy Returns and local same-day or large-item deliveries through Roadie.
